paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches. Elihu says Job's sin or Job's righteousness can't add to God or take from Him, and that it touches only "a man like yourself" (Job 35:8). I think that sounds cold at first, so let me say it plainly: God is so far above us that He needs nothing from us. He isn't a boss waiting on our performance reports.

Now look at the other half, because Elihu doesn't stop there. He says no one asks, "Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night" (Job 35:10). When life gets heavy, it's easy to stare at the pain and the people who caused it and forget to look up at the One who made us. Then Elihu says that what Job claims about God, that his case is before Him and he must wait, is "words without knowledge" (Job 35:14, 16).

So here's what I want you to bake into your day, friend. When you're hurting, be honest, but ask "Where is God my Maker?" before you start writing the speech. And remember, this is Elihu talking, a younger man who waited to speak (Job 32:2-4), so we hold his words up against the rest of Job's story. It isn't over, and I'm telling you, there's MORE coming.
